target_customer: Pharmaceutical, wellness and supplement companies and research customers that buy rare cannabinoids, terpenes and tryptamines made by fermentation
problem: Rare cannabinoids exist at tiny levels in the plant, and plant growth takes months with pesticide, heavy metal and consistency issues; fermentation from sugar promises cleaner, cheaper supply.
business_model: Ingredient sales and R&D partnerships, plus a joint venture (TryptageniX with atai Life Sciences)
product_category: Synthetic biology and precision fermentation of natural products

founders.name: Sher Ali Butt
prior_employers: Steep Hill (cannabis testing lab, CSO per company site)
education: MBA (school not stated on company site)
previous_startups: CB Labs (cannabis testing lab, per company site)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2018 says he had the idea while at Steep Hill and worked on it on and off for years.

founders.name: Jacob Vogan
education: PhD (field and school not stated on company site)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2018 calls him an old college friend of Butt working in bioengineering; company site cites papers and patents in alkaloid biosynthesis and precision fermentation.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reconstructing plant biosynthesis pathways in yeast and scaling fermentation for dozens of rare compounds is research-grade metabolic engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Company says the pathways it developed are its main intellectual property and patents are pending; other synthetic biology firms were pursuing similar routes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company stayed independent and formed a joint venture with atai Life Sciences announced in December 2021.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in September 2018 noted regulatory and testing hurdles and uncertain pricing, with demand driven by interest in rare cannabinoids beyond THC and CBD; no hard spend data found.

branding.brand_signature: The PsyVault collection of biosynthetic cannabinoids and psychedelics, named in search coverage

brand_strength.rationale: Name reads as CB for cannabinoid and no longer fits as the focus moved to psychedelics and AI; coverage focuses on science, not brand.

pivots.to: Psychedelic tryptamines such as psilocybin and DMT, later AI-driven healthspan therapeutics
pivots.why: Announced first biosynthetic psilocybin and tryptamines and a joint venture with atai; the reason is not stated in opened sources.

outcome_analysis: CB Therapeutics launched at TechCrunch Disrupt in September 2018, raised a 7.5 million dollar first equity round in April 2019 and a Series A fully taken by re.Mind Capital in May 2021, then moved into psychedelic compounds and a joint venture with atai. It is still operating, but revenue and total funding are unverified, so the result is a surviving deep tech company with unclear traction.
notes: Series A in May 2021 is from search results quoting Business Wire and BioSpace; the Business Wire page was blocked (403) so the amount is not known. The 2019 round label is the source's own wording (first round of equity funding), recorded as other; investors not named. Seedtable lists an August 2018 round of about 120K, unverified aggregator. The 2018 TechCrunch launch article names no competitors; 2019 articles naming Demetrix and Hyasynth are too late for as_of, so the list is empty. YC page says San Diego, company site says Carlsbad. A MarketScreener profile naming another founder and 2015 is contradicted by other sources and ignored.
